title: Why AMI Labs’ Alexandre LeBrun won’t call his AI ‘AGI’ or ‘superintelligence’
slides: LeBrun built an AI. Why won't he name it AGI?
Most labs race to claim superintelligence benchmarks.
LeBrun says his system fails a simple childhood test.
You must stop trusting AI rankings that ignore limits.
Test your own model on one question it cannot answer.
thread_text:
1. Why won't he call it AGI?

LeBrun's AI fails a test most 4-year-olds pass. He still won't use the word "superintelligence."

2. Labs race to claim benchmarks

Every major lab claims their model just hit superintelligence. None publish the test their system flunks.

3. The test his AI botched

He asked it to explain why a ball falls when dropped. The model gave physics — then contradicted itself.

4. Trust the rankings less

If a leaderboard ignores simple failure cases like this one, it's marketing, not science. Don't treat it as proof.

5. Ask your model this today

Take your current favorite AI and ask: "Why does this object sink?" If it dodges or flips, you know its real limit.
